links.outcome: Token retention of AI drafts across prompt refinement phases
links.effect: Prompt refinements (Phases 2–4 vs Phase 1) increased token retention of drafts in final physician messages.

links.outcome: Flesch Reading Ease of AI drafts vs final physician-sent messages
links.effect: Final physician messages were longer and more readable than GPT drafts; authors cite readability challenges.
links.quote: Final messages were longer and more readable.

unlisted_practices: Using automated semantic similarity metrics (BERTScore) paired with physician feedback to evaluate AI-drafted messages

openai.sample_unit: GPT-generated draft replies to patient portal messages

links.outcome: Clinician uptake of AI-generated patient-message drafts
links.effect: Of 66,200 generated drafts, 21,073 were presented and 2,264 (11%) were used, documenting low uptake without establishing its cause.
links.quote: Of 66,200 GDRs generated, 21,073 were presented, and 2,264 (11%) were used.

unlisted_practices: Refining patient-message drafting prompts to increase draft-token retention in final replies.
Validating BERTScore against physician evaluations as a proxy for reply effectiveness and safety.
Evaluating semantic alignment between AI drafts and final clinician messages using automated metrics like BLEU and BERTScore
Monitoring utilization and edit rates of AI draft replies over time in clinical workflows
